title: Where must the sum of two decimals lie?
description: The sums of 25.936 with 8.202, and of 25.93603259 with 8.202, are checked against a claim about the whole parts total and two more. Keeko doubts the result and thinks the sum is exactly 33.
teaching_notes: One idea: the whole parts give the low end, and the fractional parts add under two. Watch for students who ignore the fractional parts.

source: Check Sonu's claim for 25.936 and 8.202, and for 25.93603259
video_script.why: The child can add decimals and now uses the whole parts to say where a sum must lie.
video_script.substitution: Add the whole parts for the low end, add two more for the high end, and check the sum lies between them.
video_script.anchor: The numbers 25.936, 25.93603259 and 8.202 on a number line, with the range 33 to 35 marked as a band.
video_script.wrong_answer: the sum is exactly thirty three
video_script.wrong_move: Says the sum is exactly 33, the total of the whole parts, and ignores the fractional parts.
video_script.payoff_line: The whole parts give the range, and the fractional parts add under two

final_answer.value: 34.138 and 34.13803259 both lie between 33 and 35; the claim holds for any two decimals, with 'equal to' allowed at the low end
final_answer.spoken: thirty four point one three eight and thirty four point one three eight zero three two five nine both lie between thirty three and thirty five; the claim holds for any two decimals, with equal to allowed at the low end

names.{{NAME_1}}: claims a sum of two decimals lies between the whole parts total and two more

hold_back: 34.138 and 34.13803259 both lie between 33 and 35; the claim holds for any two decimals, with 'equal to' allowed at the low end
maths_rules: each fractional part is under 1, so two together are under 2
the sum equals 33 only when both fractional parts are zero, so the claim should read 'greater than or equal to'
video_script.design: A number line shows a band from 33 to 35. Each sum lands in the band as a bead, and the fractional parts are drawn as short bars.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the claim and the numbers 25.936 and 8.202

marks.claim: the first half of the claim appears
marks.claim2: the second half of the claim appears
marks.ask: the two decimals appear with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about estimating sums.
<bookmark mark='claim'/>{{NAME_1}} says a sum of two decimals is greater than the sum of their whole parts.
<bookmark mark='claim2'/>The sum is also less than two more than that.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is this true for twenty five point nine three six and eight point two zero two?

beats.on_screen: the claim and the two decimals stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: whole part = before the point; fractional part = after the point, less than 1

marks.whole: the digits before the point glow
marks.frac: the digits after the point glow and a bar shorter than one appears

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>The whole part of a decimal is the number before the point.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>The fractional part comes after the point, and it is always less than one.

marks.g2: the second pair is written below it

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twenty five point nine three six and eight point two zero two.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Then the first number grows longer. It becomes twenty five point nine three six zero three two five nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: does each sum lie between the whole parts total and 2 more?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to check the claim for both pairs.

marks.low: the band starts at thirty three on the number line
marks.high: the band ends at thirty five

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step one, find the range. The whole parts are twenty five and eight, and they total thirty three.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Add one to each, and the total is thirty five. The claim says the sum lies between thirty three and thirty five.

marks.f1: the two fractional bars are shown
marks.f2: the bars join and the sum bead is placed
marks.f3: the bead sits inside the band

narration: <bookmark mark='f1'/>Step two, add the first pair. The fractional parts are zero point nine three six and zero point two zero two.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>Together they make one point one three eight. Thirty three plus that is thirty four point one three eight.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>It is above thirty three and below thirty five.

marks.l1: the long fractional bar is shown
marks.l2: the sum bead is placed just beside the first bead
marks.l3: the bead sits inside the band

narration: <bookmark mark='l1'/>Step three, the longer number. Its fractional part is zero point nine three six zero three two five nine.
<bookmark mark='l2'/>That gives one point one three eight zero three two five nine. The sum is thirty four point one three eight zero three two five nine.
<bookmark mark='l3'/>It also lies between thirty three and thirty five.

beats.on_screen: each fractional part < 1, so two together < 2; the sum is 33 or more, equal only if both are 0

marks.w1: two bars shorter than one are placed end to end
marks.w2: the low end of the band is marked equal to

narration: <bookmark mark='w1'/>Step four, why does this hold for any two decimals? Each fractional part is less than one, so two of them together are less than two.
<bookmark mark='w2'/>That keeps the sum below thirty five. It equals thirty three only when both fractional parts are zero.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 34.138 and 34.13803259 both lie between 33 and 35; the claim holds for any two decimals, with 'equal to' allowed at the low end

marks.v1: both beads are ticked inside the band
marks.v2: the low end of the band is marked equal to

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The whole parts give the range, and the fractional parts add under two.
<bookmark mark='v1'/>Thirty four point one three eight and the longer sum both lie between thirty three and thirty five.
<bookmark mark='v2'/>The claim holds for any two decimals, if equal to is allowed at the low end.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: the sum is exactly 33; the fractional parts add 1.138; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the fractional bars are added above thirty three

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sum is exactly thirty three, the total of the whole parts.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the fractional parts add something more.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The sum is above thirty three, unless both fractional parts are zero.
